note: Candidate variables for environmental trend investigations. Collection identifiers, versions, variable names and record start dates were not re-checked against Earthdata Search for this draft (checked: false). Confirm each in Earthdata Search or Giovanni before building an adapter.

variables.label: Nitrogen dioxide (tropospheric column)
variables.plainDefinition: How much nitrogen dioxide gas sits in the lower atmosphere above an area. Most of it comes from burning fuel: traffic, power plants and backup generators.
caveats: A column through the atmosphere, not the concentration at breathing height.
Cloudy days are screened out, so some months have few valid days.
OMI has a known row anomaly since 2007 that reduces coverage.

variables.label: Aerosol optical thickness (model reanalysis)
variables.plainDefinition: How much haze, smoke, dust and fine particles block sunlight, estimated by a NASA model that combines satellite and other observations.
caveats: A model estimate of the whole air column, not a surface PM2.5 measurement.
Coarse grid cells can be larger than the area around a single facility.

variables.label: Aerosol optical depth (satellite)
variables.plainDefinition: A satellite measurement of how hazy the air is from particles such as smoke, dust and pollution.
caveats: Column measurement, not surface air quality.
Clear-sky retrievals only.

variables.label: Air temperature at 2 metres (model reanalysis)
variables.plainDefinition: The air temperature about head height above the ground, as estimated by a NASA model built from many observations.
caveats: Regional climate signal; cells are far larger than a facility site.

variables.label: Daytime land surface temperature
variables.plainDefinition: How hot the ground, roofs and vegetation surfaces are in the daytime, measured from space. Built-up areas are often hotter than fields or forests.
caveats: Surface skin temperature, not air temperature.
Clear-sky only; apply the quality flags.
Apply the scale factor before analysis.

variables.label: Precipitation
variables.plainDefinition: How much rain and snow falls, combined from many satellites.
caveats: Rainfall is year-to-year noisy; trends often need long records to become significant.

variables.label: Topsoil moisture (0-10 cm)
variables.plainDefinition: How much water is held in the top layer of soil, which crops and plants draw on.
caveats: A land-model estimate driven by observations, not a direct soil measurement.
Does not include a facility's own water withdrawals.

variables.label: Evapotranspiration
variables.plainDefinition: Water returning to the air from soil, water surfaces and plant leaves.
caveats: Model estimate; it does not separate cooling-tower evaporation from natural evaporation.

variables.label: Total water storage (including groundwater)
variables.plainDefinition: Changes in all water stored on and under the land - soil, groundwater, lakes and snow - detected from tiny changes in Earth's gravity.
caveats: Very coarse; reflects whole regions, never a single site.
Gap between the two missions (2017-2018) must be reported as missing.

variables.label: Vegetation greenness (NDVI)
variables.plainDefinition: A satellite index of how green and leafy plants are. Healthy crops and forests score high; bare ground and pavement score low.
caveats: Greenness is an indicator of vegetation condition, not a measurement of crop yield.
Apply quality flags and the scale factor.

variables.label: Land cover type
variables.plainDefinition: What covers the ground each year - cropland, forest, grassland, water or built-up land.
variables.units: class (analyze as the share of a class in the region)
caveats: Categorical; trend-test the yearly share of one class (for example built-up land), not class codes.
Year-to-year classification noise can mimic change.

variables.label: River and lake water quality
variables.plainDefinition: Chemistry and temperature of local rivers and lakes.
variables.unavailableReason: No suitable NASA trend variable for small inland waters near facilities. Needs ground sampling records (for example the Water Quality Portal) and a dedicated adapter.

variables.label: Environmental noise
variables.plainDefinition: Sound levels heard near homes and habitats.
variables.unavailableReason: Satellites do not measure sound. Needs ground acoustic measurements and an acoustic propagation model.
